primary_topics: Welcome address by CJP on behalf of the Manila Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica Foundation at the 5th organ concert in a series featuring the Cathedral's renovated giant pipe organ, November 12, 2010

The Manila Cathedral's identity: 'bulwark of Filipino Catholicism and an enduring witness to the strength and depth of our people's fidelity to our Lord Jesus Christ' -- founded 1581; damaged multiple times; Neo-Romanesque Byzantine architecture designed by Fernando Ocampo; reconstructed by Archbishop Rufino Santos (first Filipino Cardinal); consecrated December 7, 1958

The current restoration context: belfry heavy bells brought down (replaced with lighter carillon at ground level); Bert and Sylvia Lina's almost-five-million-peso gift of computerized carillon bells from the Netherlands -- to arrive for Christmas season

The 5th organ concert program: five participating choirs (UST, St. Paul's Manila, St. Scholastica's, Santa Isabel College, Manila Cathedral Choir); featured composers-organists-conductors (Buenaventura, Santiago); dance groups (Shirley Halili, St. Dominic, Pamana); TV coverage by NBN Channel 4 (Sining Gising, first Sunday of December for the Feast of the Immaculate Conception)
sub_topics: Cathedral's religious significance: 'More than mortar and brick, the Manila Cathedral is a symbol of our faith and a monument of our religious heritage as a people. It is the bulwark of Filipino Catholicism and an enduring witness to the strength and depth of our people's fidelity to our Lord Jesus Christ.'

History: from its origin in 1581; fallen to typhoons, earthquakes, fire and World War II ('practically ravaged it to the ground'); present Neo-Romanesque Byzantine structure designed by Architect Fernando Ocampo; reconstructed after WWII by Archbishop Rufino J. Santos (became the first Filipino Cardinal); consecrated December 7, 1958 under the patronage of our Mother Mary, the Immaculate Conception

Current restoration need: 'more than 50 years after its reconstruction, the Manila Cathedral needs major renovation, structural strengthening and reconstruction'; Manila Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica Foundation organized; chaired by Cardinal Gaudencio B. Cardinal Rosales

Belfry bells: 'because of frequent earthquakes, we had to bring down the giant bells on the belfry of the Cathedral and constructed a new home for them at ground level'; with financial assistance from Dr. Emilio T. Yap, the ground belfry will be finished on November 20

Bert and Sylvia Lina carillon donation: 'the Foundation has been the fortunate recipient of the generosity of Alberto and Sylvia Lina who donated almost five million pesos to acquire new computerized, top-of-the-line carillon bells from the Netherlands. They will arrive next month, so we can use them during the Christmas season.'; CJP: 'Maraming, maraming salamat po to my inaanak, Bert and Sylvia of Fedex and Air 21 fame'

Concert program: 5th in a series featuring the renovated giant pipe organ in the Cathedral balcony loft; choirs from UST, St. Paul's University of Manila, St. Scholastica's, Santa Isabel College, Manila Cathedral Choir (coordinated by Eugene de los Santos and Monsignor Nestor Cerbo); featured composers-organists-conductors: Alfredo Buenaventura and Armando Santiago; dance groups: Shirley Halili School of Ballet, St. Dominic College, Pamana; TV coverage: NBN Channel 4, Sining Gising, first Sunday of December for Feast of the Immaculate Conception

stances.claim: Bert and Sylvia Lina's donation of 'almost five million pesos' for computerized carillon bells from the Netherlands is a concrete act of Catholic stewardship -- filling the acoustic void left by the belfry bells that had to be brought down for structural safety. CJP's personal acknowledgment of them as his 'inaanak' elevates the institutional gift into a family spiritual bond.
stances.rhetorical_move: inaanak-bond as the personal dimension of institutional philanthropy: the godparent relationship making the corporate donation also a filial spiritual act

notable_anecdotes: Bert and Sylvia Lina as inaanak: CJP identifies Bert and Sylvia Lina as his godchildren ('my inaanak') -- the most personal relationship tag in the corpus for a donor. Their donation of almost P5M for Netherlands carillon bells (to arrive for Christmas 2010) was made to fill the gap left when the heavy belfry bells had to be brought down for earthquake safety.

The earthquake-driven belfry redesign: 'because of frequent earthquakes, we had to bring down the giant bells on the belfry of the Cathedral and constructed a new home for them at ground level.' Dr. Emilio T. Yap funded the ground belfry, to be finished November 20, 2010.

Cathedral's eight lives: founded 1581; 'damaged eight times but had been rebuilt, reconstructed and/or restored eight times too' (from SC077 context); this 2010 speech occurs during the third act of the restoration -- before the full two-year retrofit narrated in SC077 (2014).

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 12, 2010 as the welcome address on behalf of the Manila Metropolitan Cathedral-Basilica Foundation at the 5th organ concert featuring the Cathedral's renovated giant pipe organ, this address by CJP opens with the governing theological frame: 'More than mortar and brick, the Manila Cathedral is a symbol of our faith and a monument of our religious heritage as a people. It is the bulwark of Filipino Catholicism and an enduring witness to the strength and depth of our people's fidelity to our Lord Jesus Christ.' He traces the Cathedral's history from its 1581 founding through typhoons, earthquakes, fire and WWII ('practically ravaged it to the ground'); the current Neo-Romanesque Byzantine structure was designed by Architect Fernando Ocampo and reconstructed after WWII by Archbishop Rufino J. Santos -- who became the first Filipino Cardinal -- and consecrated December 7, 1958 under the patronage of Mary, the Immaculate Conception. Now, 50+ years after reconstruction, major renovation is needed; the Foundation is chaired by Cardinal Rosales. Recent work: the giant belfry bells were brought down for earthquake safety and housed at ground level (with Dr. Emilio T. Yap's funding; to be finished November 20, 2010). And: 'the Foundation has been the fortunate recipient of the generosity of Alberto and Sylvia Lina who donated almost five million pesos to acquire new computerized, top-of-the-line carillon bells from the Netherlands. They will arrive next month, so we can use them during the Christmas season. Maraming, maraming salamat po to my inaanak, Bert and Sylvia of Fedex and Air 21 fame.' The concert program features choirs from UST, St. Paul's, St. Scholastica's, Santa Isabel and the Manila Cathedral Choir (coordinated by Eugene de los Santos and Monsignor Nestor Cerbo), composers-organists Buenaventura and Santiago, dance groups (Shirley Halili, St. Dominic, Pamana), and TV coverage by NBN Channel 4 for the Feast of the Immaculate Conception.
